slides.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline: fix gross margin and delivery economics, not headcount

paragraphs.text: Reversing Harlow's margin decline: fix gross margin and delivery economics, not headcount
Diagnosis, recommended margin plan and first moves to reach a 3.0% operating margin by FY2028 · Board meeting, February 2027 · Prepared for Dana Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer
Harlow Fresh Markets
Board of directors (presented by the CEO)
Board confidential · synthetic benchmark data

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix gross margin and delivery, not headcount: seven firm levers lift margin from 1.0% to about 2.6% by FY2028, and a second wave prepared now closes the gap to 3.0%
Promotions, shrink and home delivery drove the 2.35-percentage-point fall; wages explain only 13%
–	Gross margin and e-commerce explain 79% of the fall; productivity offset two-thirds of the wage rise
–	Fully costed, e-commerce loses about $10M a year, not the 6.1% margin reported
The draft 8% labor cut and e-commerce freeze would leave FY2028 margin near 1.1%, far short of 3.0%
–	The cut saves $14.5M on paper, but lean stores run 3.1% shrink against 2.3%: we expect $4–8M back, before lost sales
Seven firm levers (about $30M) reach about 2.6%; about half of a ~$10M second wave closes the gap
–	Gross margin $16.9M · targeted labor $5.5M · delivery $3.3M · exit 6 lease-expiry stores $4.4M (range $17–38M)
–	Wave 2: exit 3 more stores (board vote), cost-recovery delivery, vendor funding to 55%
Four no-regret moves in 90 days lift FY2026 income to about $25M, about $5M above the covenant
–	Promotion reset · delivery pricing · targeted labor · notice on 6 lease-expiry stores; about $17M one-time, within $25M
Key risks are ValuMart traffic and vendor push-back; we ask the board for three decisions
–	Endorse the plan, not the 8% cut · approve delivery repricing · prepare the 3-store vote
–	If wave 2 falls short, click-and-collect only reaches about 3.0% but needs the owners' consent

slides.title: Against seven tests, the margin-first diagnosis held, but its first answer fell short of the margin target

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Options    3 Plan    4 First moves    5 Risks & asks
Against seven tests, the margin-first diagnosis held, but its first answer fell short of the margin target
Starting hypothesis: a gross-margin and delivery problem, not a wage problem, fixed by promotions and delivery pricing rather than labor cuts

data: What would have to be true, tested against the pack
1. Gross margin and e-commerce drove it
Gross margin −1.02 pp and e-commerce −0.84 pp: 79% of the fall; store labor −0.30 pp: 13% (p.5)
2. Promotion is not buying profitable traffic
38% of events lost money; +5 pp of promo share costs $10.5M a year and needs about $53M of new sales (p.6–7)
−$10.4M with delivery and 70% cannibalization: −$12.34 per delivery, −$1.64 per pickup (p.9)
Fee test: delivered −9%, click-and-collect +14%, sales −2%; about $2.5M a year, a quarter of the loss (p.13)
5. An 8% hours cut costs no shrink or service
Management view. Leanest quartile: 3.1% shrink against 2.3%; shrink +0.5 pp as hours per sales fell 6% (p.8)
6. Weak stores can exit within commitments
6 of the 9 negative-EBITDA stores have leases ending by 2027: no vote needed; about $4.4M a year (p.14)
Promotions and delivery: about $13M; all seven levers about $30M (2.6%); about $5M more from a second wave (p.15)

paragraphs.text: Revised answer: add shrink, targeted labor and store exits, and prepare a second wave to reach 3.0%

slides.title: Closing six stores at lease end by 2027 adds about $4.4M a year with no vote; the other three take 3.4 years to repay

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Options    3 Plan    4 First moves    5 Risks & asks
Closing six stores at lease end by 2027 adds about $4.4M a year with no vote; the other three take 3.4 years to repay
The nine loss-making stores (negative four-wall EBITDA), $ millions, FY2025
Why not exit all nine now?
▪	Vote, cash, payback: the other 3 need a board vote and $7.5M (44% of the one-time budget), and repay slower than any lever
▪	Gain likely understated: depreciation also goes on exit; overheads that stay are already outside four-wall EBITDA
▪	Pro-rata split: if the 6 carry less loss, the gain could be about $3M
Give notice on the 6 now; test a cheap fix in the other 3 for six months, with a board vote in mid-FY2027 if it fails
1  Pro-rata split (6/9, 3/9): the pack gives only totals. Closures: $0.5M a store (team allowance). Confirm store P&Ls before notice; the other 3 are wave 2
